newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan foreign equity cap to rise on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan foreign equity cap to rise on Thursday.

text.p: A reform easing the upper limit on foreign ownership of Taiwan stock-market equity to 25 percent from 20 percent will take effect on Thursday, the Securities and Exchange Commission said.
The liberalisation also relaxes the ceiling of a single foreign investment on any one listed company to 10 percent from 7.5 percent, the market watchdog said in a statement.
The finance ministry and the central bank announced the reforms on September 23 but gave no implementation date, saying only that they would take effect in 1996.
The government plans gradually to remove barriers to foreign investment in Taiwan's financial markets as part of its drive to develop the island into an Asia-Pacific financial centre.

When Taiwan's share market was first opened to foreign investment several years ago, the equity ceilings were conceived to ensure local control of Taiwan firms and to stabilise the local financial markets.
Foreign ownership of local equity remains below 10 percent and raising the cap was unlikely to have an immediate impact.
